elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: § 8.2 as rendered still provides automatic renewal ("Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives sixty (60) days' advance written notice") rather than renewal by mutual written agreement, and the conditional automatic-renewal elements are not all satisfied (opt-out window is 60 days, not 30; no Vendor reminder). To meet this element the drafter must either require mutual written agreement to renew or reduce the opt-out to 30 days and add a 60-day pre-renewal Vendor reminder obligation.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: § 8.2: "Each Order Form renews for twelve months" — the renewal term equals 12 months, the maximum permitted.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 8.2 requires "sixty (60) days' advance written notice" to prevent renewal; that exceeds the preferred 30-day maximum. Repair by changing the notice period in § 8.2 to thirty (30) days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder mechanic appears anywhere in §§ 8.2–8.3; the only Vendor notice obligation is the 90 days' notice of a Fee increase in § 8.3, which is a pricing notice, not a renewal reminder. Repair by inserting an express obligation on Vendor to notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before the renewal date.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: § 8.3 (unchanged): "Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent." This is exactly the lesser-of-CPI-and-3% formulation.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 8.2 shortens the window from one hundred eighty days to "sixty (60) days' advance written notice", which is at (not above) the 60-day fallback maximum; the deterministic check "non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days" also passed.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at "the lesser of" CPI and "three percent", which is within the 5% fallback ceiling; no change was needed.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single edit brings the non-renewal notice window to exactly 60 days, and the pre-existing § 8.3 CPI/3% cap already sits inside the 5% fallback ceiling.

Preferred level is not reached: the opt-out remains 60 days rather than 30, and no 60-day pre-renewal Vendor reminder obligation exists. Targeting the fallback is a legitimate choice, but the drafter should note these as preferred-only gaps (as the rationale does) rather than claim preferred coverage.

The original 180-day window exceeded the 90-day walk-away threshold, so classifying the clause as a deviation and redlining it is correct; the 12-month renewal term was already compliant and was properly left untouched.

Minimality holds: only the numeral in § 8.2 changed (one hundred eighty days → sixty (60) days). § 8.3's uplift cap, 90-day increase notice, and prepaid-period protection — all Customer-favourable — were retained verbatim, and no survival tails, procedures, or extraneous requirements were added. The added parenthetical numeral sits inside the words being replaced and is not a separate cosmetic edit.

Intent is preserved: the mutual "either Party" structure, the Order Form-level renewal mechanic, the twelve-month renewal term, and all pricing timing mechanics survive without contradiction; no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.
